problems.quote: constituted by the Constitution (Inter‑State Council) Act, 1990
problems.problem: The Inter-State Council was constituted by a Presidential Order in 1990, not by an Act of Parliament.
problems.correction: constituted by a Presidential Order in 1990
problems.verifierReason: Inter-State Council created by Presidential Order (28 May 1990) under Art. 263, not by an Act.

problems.quote: Union Home Minister (as chairperson)
problems.problem: The Inter-State Council is chaired by the Prime Minister, not the Union Home Minister.
problems.correction: Prime Minister (as chairperson)
problems.verifierReason: PM is Chairman of Inter-State Council; Home Minister is Vice-Chairman.

problems.quote: 14th Finance Commission (2007‑12) suggested that 32 % of the net proceeds of taxes should be allocated to the states
problems.problem: The 14th Finance Commission's term was 2015-2020 and it recommended 42% devolution; the 13th Finance Commission (2010-2015) recommended 32%.
problems.correction: 13th Finance Commission (2010‑15) suggested that 32 % of the net proceeds of taxes should be allocated to the states
problems.verifierReason: 13th FC (2010-15) recommended 32% devolution; 14th FC (2015-20) recommended 42%.

problems.quote: 15th Finance Commission (2017‑22) introduced the “State Finance Commission” concept, recommending a “Performance‑Based Grant”
problems.problem: The 15th Finance Commission's term is 2020-2025; State Finance Commissions are constitutional bodies under Article 243-I, not introduced by the 15th FC.
problems.correction: 15th Finance Commission (2020‑25) recommended performance-based grants for local bodies
problems.verifierReason: 15th FC term is 2020-25; SFCs are constitutional (Art. 243-I/Y), not introduced by 15th FC.

problems.quote: The Commission’s recommendations are binding on the Union
problems.problem: Finance Commission recommendations are advisory, not binding on the Union.
problems.correction: The Commission’s recommendations are advisory but generally accepted by the Union
problems.verifierReason: FC recommendations are advisory (Art. 280), not binding, though usually accepted.

problems.quote: mandated that any proclamation of President’s Rule be subject to judicial review within two months
problems.problem: The S.R. Bommai judgment mandated that the proclamation is subject to judicial review; the two-month period refers to parliamentary approval, not judicial review.
problems.correction: mandated that any proclamation of President’s Rule be subject to judicial review and must be approved by Parliament within two months
problems.verifierReason: Bommai: proclamation subject to judicial review; 2-month limit is for parliamentary approval.

problems.quote: the 103rd Amendment’s 10 % EWS quota only to the extent it violated the 50 % ceiling (Jarnail Singh v. Lachhmi Narain Gupta, 2018)
problems.problem: The case citation and outcome are incorrect. Jarnail Singh v. Lachhmi Narain Gupta (2018) concerns creamy layer in SC/ST promotions, not the EWS quota. The 103rd Amendment (2019) providing 10% EWS quota was upheld by the Supreme Court in Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India (2022), not struck down for v
problems.correction: the 103rd Amendment’s 10 % EWS quota was upheld as not violating the 50 % ceiling (Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India, 2022)
problems.verifierReason: Original quote cites wrong case (Jarnail Singh is SC/ST creamy layer) and wrong outcome. Correction cites correct case (Janhit Abhiyan 2022) and correct outcome (upheld).

problems.quote: 12 service packages beyond maternal-child health: NCD screening/management, mental health, ENT, ophthalmology, dental, geriatric, palliative, and emergency care
problems.problem: The 12 Comprehensive Primary Health Care packages include maternal and child health; the list is incomplete and mischaracterized as "beyond maternal-child health".
problems.correction: 12 service packages (including maternal-child health): NCD screening/management, mental health, ENT, ophthalmology, dental, geriatric, palliative, emergency care, and others
problems.verifierReason: Original wrongly excludes maternal-child health from the 12 CPHC packages; correction accurately reflects inclusive list.

problems.quote: launched in December 2019, outlines an investment target of ₹111 lakh crore
problems.problem: The National Infrastructure Pipeline (NIP) was launched in December 2019 with an investment target of ₹102 lakh crore; the ₹111 lakh crore figure was announced later (in the 2021‑22 Budget).
problems.correction: launched in December 2019, outlines an investment target of ₹102 lakh crore
problems.verifierReason: NIP launched Dec 2019 with ₹102L cr target; ₹111L cr announced in Budget 2021-22

problems.quote: created the Catastrophe Containment and Relief Trust
problems.problem: The Catastrophe Containment and Relief Trust (CCRT) was established in 2015, not created in response to the COVID-19 pandemic.
problems.correction: utilized the Catastrophe Containment and Relief Trust
problems.verifierReason: CCRT established Feb 2015 for Ebola; activated/modified for COVID-19 in 2020. Original implies creation during pandemic.

problems.quote: The grants are divided into two components: (i) basic grants, which are untied and distributed on the basis of population (90 % weight) and area (10 % weight), and (ii) performance grants, which are c
problems.problem: The 15th Finance Commission recommended a two-component structure (basic + performance grants) only for Urban Local Bodies. Rural Local Bodies receive only basic (untied) grants; there are no performance grants for RLBs. The text incorrectly implies this division applies to the total grant pool cove
problems.correction: For urban local bodies, the grants are divided into two components: (i) basic grants, which are untied and distributed on the basis of population (90 % weight) and area (10 % weight), and (ii) perform
problems.verifierReason: Original implies two-component grants for all local bodies; 15th FC only has performance grants for ULBs, RLBs get only basic grants.

problems.quote: The Commission's recommendation to allocate 4.31 % of the divisible pool of taxes to local bodies (up from 3.54 % under the 14th FC) marks a substantial increase
problems.problem: The 14th Finance Commission also recommended 4.31% of the divisible pool for local bodies (not 3.54%). The 15th FC maintained the same percentage share (4.31%); the increase was in absolute quantum due to a larger divisible pool.
problems.correction: The Commission's recommendation to allocate 4.31 % of the divisible pool of taxes to local bodies (the same share as under the 14th FC) marks a substantial increase in absolute quantum.
problems.verifierReason: 14th FC recommended 4.31% of divisible pool, not 3.54%; 15th FC maintained same share; increase is in absolute terms.

problems.quote: The Supreme Court’s “trade‑secret” exception, articulated in Infosys Ltd. v. Competition Commission (2022)
problems.problem: No Supreme Court ruling in Infosys Ltd. v. Competition Commission (2022) articulates a trade‑secret exception; the trade‑secret exemption under RTI Act stems from CBSE v. Aditya Bandopadhyay (2011).
problems.correction: The Supreme Court’s trade‑secret exception under RTI Act (CBSE v. Aditya Bandopadhyay, 2011)
problems.verifierReason: No SC judgment 'Infosys Ltd v CCI (2022)' on trade-secret exception; CBSE v Aditya Bandopadhyay (2011) is the correct RTI precedent.

problems.quote: Section 13 of the MGNREGA Act, which mandates “social audit of the implementation of the scheme at the district level.”
problems.problem: Section 13 of MGNREGA mandates social audit at Gram Panchayat level, not district level.
problems.correction: Section 13 of the MGNREGA Act, which mandates “social audit of the implementation of the Scheme in every Gram Panchayat.”
problems.verifierReason: MGNREGA Sec 13 mandates social audit at Gram Panchayat level, not district level.

problems.quote: algorithmic transparency (Section 23 of DPDP Act)
problems.problem: DPDP Act, 2023 does not contain a Section 23 on algorithmic transparency; Section 23 establishes the Data Protection Board.
problems.correction: algorithmic transparency (not provided in DPDP Act)
problems.verifierReason: DPDP Act 2023 Sec 23 establishes Data Protection Board; no provision on algorithmic transparency exists.

problems.quote: DPDP 23 demands dynamic “logic explanations.”
problems.problem: DPDP Act Section 23 does not demand logic explanations; the Act has no provision for algorithmic logic explanations.
problems.correction: DPDP Act does not demand logic explanations.
problems.verifierReason: DPDP Act Sec 23 does not demand logic explanations; Act lacks any algorithmic transparency requirement.

problems.quote: trade‑secret protection (Supreme Court Infosys 2022)
problems.problem: There is no Supreme Court judgment in Infosys 2022 on trade‑secret protection; the relevant precedent is CBSE v. Aditya Bandopadhyay (2011).
problems.correction: trade‑secret protection under RTI Act (2011)
problems.verifierReason: No SC 'Infosys 2022' trade-secret ruling; CBSE v Aditya Bandopadhyay (2011) is the governing RTI precedent.

problems.quote: public hearings under Section 21 of the NGT Act, 2010
problems.problem: Section 21 of the NGT Act, 2010 deals with appeals to the Supreme Court; public hearings are conducted under the EIA Notification, 2006.
problems.correction: public hearings under the EIA Notification, 2006
problems.verifierReason: NGT Act Sec 21 covers appeals to SC; public hearings are under EIA Notification 2006.

problems.quote: 29 functional as of 2023
problems.problem: There are 28 State Institutes of Rural Development (SIRDs), one per state, not 29.
problems.correction: 28 functional as of 2023
problems.verifierReason: India has 28 states as of 2023; SIRDs are one per state, so 28 is correct.

problems.quote: launched in 2020
problems.problem: The National Capacity Building Framework (NCBF) was launched in 2014, not 2020.
problems.correction: launched in 2014
problems.verifierReason: NCBF for Panchayati Raj was launched by MoPR in 2014, not 2020.

problems.quote: creation of a Chief Electoral Officer for Panchayati Raj elections
problems.problem: The Ashok Mehta Committee recommended a State Election Commission for Panchayati Raj elections, not a Chief Electoral Officer.
problems.correction: creation of a State Election Commission for Panchayati Raj elections
problems.verifierReason: Ashok Mehta Committee (1978) recommended State Election Commission for Panchayat polls.

problems.quote: Second Administrative Reforms Commission (2008)
problems.problem: The Second ARC’s report on local governance was submitted in 2007, not 2008.
problems.correction: Second Administrative Reforms Commission (2007)
problems.verifierReason: Second ARC's 6th report on local governance submitted 2007, not 2008.
